artifact.summary: No circuit generated. The abstract does not give the functional form of the QPA unitary U(theta), the input encoding into the initial particle state, the lattice-to-qubit embedding for 5 sites, the number of steps t, or the boundary partition. Any circuit would be an invented construction, not a reconstruction of the paper's operation.

equation_mapping.explanation: U^t evolution needs the specific U(theta), which is not given. A 5-site particle also has no specified embedding into qubits (5 basis states do not fit a power of two). A generic unitary would be arbitrary.
This is a measurement-side probability with an unspecified partition. The operation-only circuit excludes measurement and sampling.
This is a classical decision rule on measurement probabilities. It is not part of a unitary circuit, and the paper's rule is itself assumed.
GA fitness is an assumed classical optimization objective, not a quantum operation.
This is the standard majority-label definition for odd length 5. It is used only for classical evaluation and not for circuit construction.

specification_changes.change: Scope narrowed to nothing: the abstract-only specification cannot be turned into a faithful circuit, so the implementation was withheld.
specification_changes.reason: The form of U(theta), the input encoding, the qubit embedding of the 5-site lattice, t, and the boundary partition are all unspecified, and eq_3 and eq_4 are marked as assumptions in the specification.

unresolved_issues: Functional form of the QPA unitary U and the role of theta
Input encoding of the 5-bit string into the initial particle state, which the runner would have to prepare
Embedding of 5 lattice sites into qubits (for example 3 qubits with 3 unused states)
